excerpt: The household and garage tools that send the most people to the emergency room, and when a defective tool becomes a product liability claim.

faqs.question: Which garage tool causes the most serious injuries?
faqs.answer: The table saw is arguably the most dangerous tool a person can own. Its high-speed rotating blade presents a risk of laceration and amputation, and table saws account for thousands of injuries every year.

faqs.question: What injuries do common power tools cause?
faqs.answer: Tool-related accidents can result in amputation, puncture wounds, brain injury, broken bones, burn injuries and even death. The severity is often out of proportion to how routine the task felt.

faqs.question: Why do safety mechanisms not prevent these injuries?
faqs.answer: Because they do not address the most common failure. Many users skip protective eyewear, and material thrown into the eye blinds them at the moment they most need to see the rotating blade to keep clear of it.

faqs.question: Can I bring a claim if a defective tool injured me?
faqs.answer: You may be able to. Where a tool was defectively designed or manufactured, or lacked adequate warnings, a product liability claim can target the manufacturer. Preserve the tool exactly as it is after the injury.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a product liability claim in Georgia?
faqs.answer: Georgia generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit (O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33). Keeping the tool, its packaging and any manual is what makes such a claim provable.
